topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing by introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Processes, Environmental Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational causes of cancer by evaluating the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological and cellular mechanisms through which specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents drive carcinogenesis via direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, or tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Mutagenicity and Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal model, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect and evaluate carcinogenic activity.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on evaluating carcinogenic risks and benefits in daily life.
